newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea complains of rats in food aid bags.
newsitem.headline: North Korea complains of rats in food aid bags.

text.p: North Korea has complained of dead rats, twigs and lime powder in bags of corn sent by the South Korean Red Cross to help ease a food shortage in the north, a Red Cross official said on Tuesday.

The South Korean organisation has delivered 11,200 tonnes of corn to famine-threatened North Korea via China since last Thursday as part of its promise to donate 50,000 tonnes of food by the end of next month.
Rhee Jong-geun, a spokesman for the South Korean Red Cross, said North Korea on Monday lodged its complaint by telephone. He said the corn was bought in China by South Korean civic groups.

"The North said some of the packages were lighter than marked, contained dangerous levels of lime powder, chunks of dirt, stones, twigs and dead rats," said Rhee. "They asked that more attention be paid to prevent such an occurrence."

The Korea Sharing Movement, which is campaigning in South Korea to raise funds to aid the communist North, said Chinese companies that sold the corn had apologised for "making packaging mistakes" and agreed to compensate.
Rhee said nine South Korean Red Cross officials left Seoul on Tuesday for China to oversee the delivery of the second batch of aid totalling 17,600 tonnes.
International aid agencies have warned that North Korea desperately needs large-scale food aid to avert severe famine caused by years of economic decline and two years of devastating floods.
North and South Korea have been technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce rather than a peace treaty.
